speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You have presented with generalized fatigue, mild fever, abdominal pain, and nausea. To begin my assessment, have you noticed any specific changes in your bowel habits, such as diarrhea or constipation, or any blood in your stool?

speaker: Patient
text: 47-year-old female. The patient describes a 3-week history of generalized fatigue, mild fever, abdominal pain, and nausea. She recalls attending the state fair over a month ago where she tried various regional foods. Recently, she has observed the darkening of her urine, which she believes is due to inadequate water intake. She has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Hepatitis A (likely acquired at the state fair). The combination of fever, abdominal pain, nausea, and dark urine in a diabetic patient is highly suggestive of viral hepatitis. I will order liver function tests and serology to confirm. REQUEST TEST: LFT, HAV-IgM, Hepatitis B & C panel. REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal Ultrasound.
